record.paper_title: Developments and open problems on chiral polytopes
record.original_question: Determine which noncompact surfaces without boundary admit embeddings of chiral maps.

evidence.quote: Problem 22 Determine which noncompact surfaces without boundary admit embeddings of chiral maps.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A map is an embedding of a connected graph into a surface (without boundary) such that each connected component of the complement is homeomorphic to an open disc; the cells of the map are the vertices, edges, and faces. An automorphism of a map is a permutation of its cells that preserves incidences; the automorphism group acts semi-regularly on the set of flags (mutually incident vertex-edge-face triples). The map is called regular if the automorphism group acts transitively (hence regularly) on flags. On an orientable surface, the orientation-preserving automorphisms form a subgroup of index at most 2; a map on an orientable surface is called orientably regular if this subgroup acts regularly on the set of darts (or arcs). An orientably regular map is called chiral if it is not isomorphic to its mirror image, equivalently, if it admits no orientation-reversing automorphism.

A noncompact surface without boundary is a connected 2-manifold without boundary that is not compact (for instance, the plane, the cylinder, the Loch Ness monster surface, a surface with infinitely many ends, etc.).

Problem: Characterize, up to homeomorphism, those noncompact surfaces without boundary that admit an embedding of a chiral map.
artifact.status_search_result: No published resolution was located. The problem appears in a list of open problems on chiral polytopes/maps and standard search results focus on chiral maps on compact (closed) surfaces or chiral covers; no work characterizing which noncompact surfaces without boundary support chiral map embeddings was found. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Chiral covers of regular maps of given type
status_evidence.snippet: Every orientably-regular reflexible map of arbitrary non-spherical type has infinitely many orientably-regular but chiral smooth covers.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work on chiral maps focuses on covers of regular maps on closed surfaces, not on classifying noncompact surfaces admitting chiral maps.

status_evidence.title: Graph Embeddings and Maps on Surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Maps on surfaces, regular and chiral maps.
status_evidence.claim: Contemporary research on chiral maps continues to concentrate on compact surfaces, leaving the noncompact case unresolved.
